concepts.name: User flow diagrams
concepts.summary: Explain how a user flow maps the steps and decisions a person takes from entry point to goal across screens.

concepts.name: Visual hierarchy cues
concepts.summary: Recognise how size, contrast, colour, spacing and position direct attention to the most important elements.

concepts.name: Common UI components
concepts.summary: Name and recognise buttons, form fields, menus, cards, modals and tabs and state what each is for.

concepts.name: Wireframe fidelity levels
concepts.summary: Describe how low-fidelity wireframes, mockups and prototypes differ in purpose and detail.

concepts.name: Alignment and spacing
concepts.summary: Understand how alignment, consistent spacing and grouping make related items read as a unit and screens feel orderly.

concepts.name: Figma frames and layers
concepts.summary: Remember how frames, shapes, text and layers are organised on a Figma canvas.

concepts.name: Core accessibility needs
concepts.summary: Explain why text contrast, readable size and non-colour cues matter for users with visual, motor and cognitive differences.

misconceptions.text: UX design is just making screens look attractive.
Wireframes should show final colours, images and polished styling.
Accessibility only matters for a small group of users with disabilities.

concepts.name: Information architecture structure
concepts.summary: Organise content into sensible groups and hierarchies using labels, categories and sitemaps.

concepts.name: Navigation pattern selection
concepts.summary: Apply patterns such as top nav, tab bar, hamburger menu and breadcrumbs appropriately to a product's size and platform.

concepts.name: Grid and layout systems
concepts.summary: Lay out screens on a column grid and adapt the layout across mobile, tablet and desktop breakpoints.

concepts.name: Typography and colour usage
concepts.summary: Apply a limited type scale and palette that support readability and convey hierarchy and state.

concepts.name: Contrast and WCAG checks
concepts.summary: Check text and UI contrast against WCAG ratios and fix failing combinations.

concepts.name: Reusable components and variants
concepts.summary: Build Figma components with variants and states so repeated elements stay consistent and editable.

concepts.name: Clickable prototype building
concepts.summary: Link frames with interactions and transitions in Figma to simulate a flow for testing.

concepts.name: Giving design feedback
concepts.summary: Describe feedback on a design in terms of user goals and observable features rather than personal taste.

misconceptions.text: A hamburger menu is a good default for any product's navigation.
Information architecture is the same as the visual menu design.
Meeting the minimum contrast ratio makes a design fully accessible.

concepts.name: Task-driven flow design
concepts.summary: Derive flows from research findings, analysing steps for friction, dead ends and unnecessary decisions.

concepts.name: Interaction states and feedback
concepts.summary: Design hover, focus, disabled, loading, empty and error states so the system always communicates its status.

concepts.name: Design token foundations
concepts.summary: Define colour, type and spacing variables so styles are applied consistently and changed centrally.

concepts.name: Keyboard and screen reader support
concepts.summary: Specify focus order, labels, headings and alt text so a screen can be used without a mouse or sight.

concepts.name: Form and input design
concepts.summary: Analyse and structure forms with sensible field order, inline validation and helpful error messages to reduce abandonment.

concepts.name: Responsive adaptation decisions
concepts.summary: Decide what to reprioritise, collapse or reflow across screen sizes rather than just scaling layouts.

concepts.name: Usability heuristic evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate screens against established heuristics to find and rank usability problems.

concepts.name: Structured design critique
concepts.summary: Run and take part in critiques that tie each decision to goals and constraints and lead to concrete revisions.

misconceptions.text: Designing only the happy path is enough for a complete flow.
Accessibility can be added at the end by running an automated checker.
Responsive design means shrinking the desktop layout to fit a phone.

concepts.name: Design system architecture
concepts.summary: Analyse how tokens, components, patterns and documentation layer together and where a system should or should not constrain designers.

concepts.name: Cognitive load management
concepts.summary: Analyse screens for load and apply progressive disclosure, chunking and defaults to reduce it.

concepts.name: Complex navigation and IA
concepts.summary: Evaluate and restructure the IA and navigation of large products using card sort, tree test and analytics evidence.

concepts.name: Accessibility conformance review
concepts.summary: Audit designs against WCAG criteria, judge severity and recommend fixes beyond automated checks.

concepts.name: Usability test-informed iteration
concepts.summary: Judge which usability findings justify design changes and prioritise revisions by severity and impact.

concepts.name: Trade-off evaluation in design
concepts.summary: Weigh competing options such as simplicity versus flexibility or consistency versus context fit using evidence and constraints.

concepts.name: Developer handoff specification
concepts.summary: Analyse what engineers need, such as states, responsive rules, tokens and edge cases, and document them so the build matches intent.

misconceptions.text: A design system guarantees good UX because everything is consistent.
Fewer options and fewer clicks always make an interface easier to use.
Every usability test finding should be fixed before release.

concepts.name: Design system strategy
concepts.summary: Judge the value, cost and governance of a design system and decide how it should evolve with product and team scale.

concepts.name: Design principles authoring
concepts.summary: Craft specific, usable principles that resolve disagreements and guide decisions for a team.

concepts.name: Cross-product experience coherence
concepts.summary: Create patterns and principles that keep flows and interfaces coherent across multiple products and platforms.

concepts.name: Design quality measurement
concepts.summary: Evaluate and select metrics such as task success, time on task and satisfaction to judge whether design changes improved the experience.

concepts.name: Critique culture leadership
concepts.summary: Evaluate and shape critique and review practices so teams produce better decisions and grow designers' judgment.

concepts.name: Inclusive design at scale
concepts.summary: Build accessibility into systems, process and tooling so inclusive outcomes are the default rather than a late fix.

concepts.name: Ethical and manipulative patterns
concepts.summary: Evaluate designs for deceptive or harmful patterns and argue for alternatives balancing business goals and user wellbeing.

misconceptions.text: Design quality can be judged by a single metric such as conversion rate.
A mature design system removes the need for design judgment on individual screens.
Critique is for senior designers to approve work.
